tasks.short: Coordinate a recall or withdrawal and sign the notice

steps.what: Log the product, the batch and the issue
Read where that batch was distributed
Confirm the batch record is the right one
Paste the notice from the logged fields
Sign the withdrawal decision and the notice
Tell the agency reviewer using that notice
Place the internal hold on the batch

tasks.design: The product owner logs product id, batch id, markets and the issue text on a {WORKFLOW} form. Distribution rows move off the {SPREADSHEET} into that record. A {DOCS} template pastes those fields into a notice and does not rewrite the issue. The specialist signs the withdrawal decision and the notice. The specialist, not a job, tells the agency reviewer. No machine posts the notice to {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Batch facts and the customer list lived in mail and a spreadsheet, so a notice could name the wrong batch.
tasks.enabler_now: Product id, batch id and markets can be fields, so the notice can paste them instead of retyping.
tasks.still_hard: Whether to withdraw, and what to say to the agency, can affect people and does not reduce to a threshold.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides to withdraw or not, signs the notice, and speaks to the agency reviewer.
tasks.altitude: Gathering the batch record takes less time. The decision, the notice and the agency conversation stay with the specialist, who can refuse to withdraw.

reach.task: Place the internal hold on the signed batch
reach.learn: Which batch ids are signed for withdrawal and which are still open

evidence.claim: A recall or market withdrawal is rare and mostly coordination and judgement. The notice can paste logged fields. The decision and the agency conversation stay with a person because a wrong notice can harm people.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so the notice pastes the issue text and does not invent a hazard line.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the specialist has signed a notice and told the agency reviewer, or has decided not to withdraw. Customer calls after the hold are out of scope.

Input contract: case id, product id, batch id, markets, issue text, distribution row id. Producer of the issue is the product owner. Producer of the batch confirmation is the quality reviewer. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual. A blank batch id stops the notice.

The meeting share in the prior fits this task. The notice template only pastes fields and does not rewrite the issue, which is why there is no writing loop. Test the native {DOCS} template and {WORKFLOW} form before any custom code. The specialist sends the notice. A machine does not.
unknowns: Who may sign a withdrawal when the specialist is absent.
Which markets require a notice as well as an internal hold.
Whether customer lists are complete for the affected batch.
research_questions: How many withdrawal cases did the firm open last year?
How often was the first notice held back for a wrong batch id?

already_counted.description: Specialist reads the pasted notice before signing
Withdrawal decision time stays with the specialist
The agency conversation stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Revise the notice template when a market needs a new field
Product owners correct a batch id the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: withdrawal notice signed for this batch id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes batch and distribution facts are still free text, so the template cannot paste them and the specialist still assembles the notice by hand. The high case assumes clean fields but the decision, the signature and the agency conversation all stay manual. Customer communication beyond the notice is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist an inspection and sign the follow-up

steps.what: State which documents the inspection needs
Pull the requested document versions
Attend the inspection with the reviewer
Draft the follow-up from marked requests

loop.input: requests the specialist marked and the notes
loop.output: follow-up items that cite request ids
loop.check: Each item cites a request id the specialist marked during or after the visit
loop.stop: Drop any item with no request id and stop after one draft
loop.why_not_simpler: The answer wording is not a field stored on the request

steps.what: Sign the follow-up version
Send the follow-up to the agency reviewer

tasks.design: The agency reviewer names document ids before and during the visit. The specialist pulls those versions from {DOCS} through a {WORKFLOW} list, instead of hunting a {SPREADSHEET}. The visit itself stays in the room. Afterwards a note in {DOCS} may answer only requests the specialist marked. The specialist signs that follow-up and sends it by {EMAIL}. Nothing is posted to {GOV_PORTAL} by a job.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requested documents were gathered from memory during the visit, and the follow-up list lived in handwritten notes.
tasks.enabler_now: A request can be a document id the specialist marks, so the follow-up can be tied to that list.
tasks.still_hard: What to say in the room, and how far to go in answering, depends on the person and the moment.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist attends the inspection and decides which follow-up promises are safe to sign.

ambition.what: Close each marked inspector request in the same week, not at the next visit

tasks.altitude: Pulling known documents takes less time. The visit and the follow-up signature stay with the specialist, who can decline a request the file does not support.

reach.task: Receive the signed follow-up for the marked requests
reach.learn: Which request ids have a signed answer and which are still open

evidence.claim: Inspection assistance is mostly the visit and the follow-up conversation. Pulling named document versions is the part that can move. A person still attends.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so a follow-up item must cite a request id the specialist marked.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task covers preparation, the visit and the signed follow-up. It does not include changing a process the inspector criticised. That is later work.

Input contract: visit id, request id, document id, document version, marked-by, due date. Producer of the request is the agency reviewer. The specialist marks which requests will be answered. A request with no document id stays on the open list. If the list is empty the specialist types the same fields from notes and marks the row manual.

Meetings and in-person time are real here, unlike desk filing. The follow-up is sent by the specialist, not by a job. Test native {DOCS} versions and the {WORKFLOW} request list before any custom code.
unknowns: How much notice the firm gets before a visit.
Who may sign a follow-up when the specialist is absent.
Which documents an inspector may see without a further check.
research_questions: What share of inspection requests name a document id on the day?
How often is a follow-up item still open a week later?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits follow-up items before signing
Time in the inspection room stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep the request list fields aligned with how visits are noted

approvals.approved_version: follow-up version signed for this visit id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requests stay as notes with no document id, so the pull rarely works and the specialist still hunts during the visit. The high case assumes named documents but the visit, the follow-up drafting and the sending all stay with the specialist. The visit itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and sign a regulatory strategy for a product

steps.what: State the product, markets and change type
Read accepted rules for those markets
Draft a path that cites those rule records

loop.input: accepted rule records and the strategy template
loop.output: outline that cites rule record ids only
loop.check: Every cited id is on the rule shortlist
loop.stop: Leave the market blank and stop that section if no record id matches
loop.why_not_simpler: The path recommendation is not a lookup from market to a fixed sentence

steps.what: Sign the regulatory strategy for this product
Read the signed path before building
Store the signed strategy on the product

tasks.design: The product owner states product id, intended markets and change type on a {WORKFLOW} form. The specialist reads accepted rule records in {DOCS} for those markets. A bounded outline may cite only those record ids. The specialist signs one strategy in a short working session, not from a {SPREADSHEET} of options. The signed path is stored on the product record. It is not sent to {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Strategy notes were rewritten from old mail, so a path could cite guidance nobody had accepted.
tasks.enabler_now: Accepted rule records have ids, so an outline can be checked against that set.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the path, including what not to claim, is a product judgement the table cannot make.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist signs the strategy and can reject an outline that cites a record they do not accept.

ambition.what: Sign the regulatory path when the product brief opens, not after the team has drafted the labeling

tasks.altitude: Less time searching for the rule. The specialist keeps the path decision and can refuse a strategy that outruns the accepted records.

reach.task: Build only what the signed strategy allows
reach.learn: Which markets and change types are on the signed path

evidence.claim: A product strategy is a judgement written down. The movable part is pulling accepted rules and drafting an outline that cites them. The path itself stays with the specialist.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so a strategy outline may cite only accepted rule record ids.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the strategy version is signed and stored. It does not file a submission.

Input contract: product id, market, change type, rule record id. Producer of the brief is the product owner. Producer of the rule records is the accepted set from the knowledge base. If a market has no accepted record the outline leaves that market blank. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields and marks the row manual.
A meeting is a real part of the signature, smaller than the document work. Test native {DOCS} templates and the {WORKFLOW} form before any custom code.
unknowns: Which markets the firm intends for the product.
Who may sign a strategy when the specialist is absent.
Whether the accepted rule set is empty for a new product type.
research_questions: What share of strategies cite a rule that was not in the accepted set?
How often is the signed path changed before the first submission?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits the outline before the path decision
Strategy signature stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Revise the strategy template when a new market block is needed
Product owners correct a market the shortlist does not cover

approvals.approved_version: regulatory strategy signed for this product id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the accepted rule set is thin, so the outline is mostly blank and the specialist still writes the path from source documents. The high case assumes clean records but every path decision is still signed in person. Later submission work is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify the standards that apply and accept the set

steps.what: Ask with product type, market and topic
List accepted records that match those fields
Accept the standards that apply to this question
Store the accepted set on the question

tasks.design: The project lead asks with product type, market and topic on a {WORKFLOW} form. An answer view in {DOCS} returns accepted records that match those three fields, including guidance, international standards and consensus standards already on the record. The specialist reads that list and accepts the set that applies. The set is stored on the question. It is not posted to {GOV_PORTAL}. A {SPREADSHEET} of links is not the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standards were found by searching loose files, so two people could name different documents for the same product question.
tasks.enabler_now: Accepted records can be matched on product type, market and topic, so the candidate list is a query.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a listed standard actually applies to this product is still a judgement. A keyword hit is not a decision.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist accepts the applicable set and can reject a hit that does not apply.

ambition.what: Project leads can ask a coded standards question and receive an accepted set without booking a meeting

tasks.altitude: Searching takes less time. The specialist still reads the candidates and can leave the set empty.

reach.task: Use only the accepted standards set on the question
reach.learn: Which record ids were accepted for this product type, market and topic

evidence.claim: Identifying guidance and standards is a search over a maintained set plus a person marking what applies. Three coded fields can list candidates. Applicability stays a person call, so this design does not use a writing model for the list.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so the candidate list may contain only accepted record ids.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when an applicable set is accepted and stored, or left empty. Maintaining the underlying records is a separate task.

Input contract: question id, product type, market, topic, rule record id. Producer of the question is the project lead. Producer of the records is the accepted knowledge base. If any of the three fields is blank the list stays empty. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields and marks the row manual.
The model prior is set aside for the list itself: a match on three fields is a query. The specialist still reads. Test the native {DOCS} list and {WORKFLOW} form before any custom code.
unknowns: Whether product type codes are stable.
Who may accept a set when the specialist is absent.
Which topics have no accepted records yet.
research_questions: What share of questions match at least one accepted record?
How often does the specialist reject every hit?

already_counted.description: Reading and applicability time stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a topic code when questions use a label the list does not know
Project leads restate a question whose three fields were blank

approvals.approved_version: applicable standards set signed for this question id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the accepted set is sparse or the question is free text, so the list is empty and the specialist still searches documents by hand. The high case assumes clean hits but every applicability decision is still signed. Building a submission from the set is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Recalls and inspections stay personal. The specialist uses the saved time to sign the notice, the follow-up and the product strategy, and to mark which standards apply.
reach: Project leads receive a signed regulatory strategy before they build the labeling.
Product owners see the applicable standards set for a coded question.
Agency reviewers receive only a follow-up or a notice the specialist has signed.
skills_to_grow: Paste a withdrawal notice from the logged batch fields and do not rewrite the issue.
Pull the document versions an inspection asked for, and keep the visit itself.
Cite a strategy only to accepted rule records.
Mark a standard as applicable only when it is already an accepted record.
role.ambitious_version: A product question returns an accepted standards set, and a strategy, a withdrawal notice or an inspection follow-up leaves only as a signed version.
